title: Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
slides: What if your next pitch deck grew a second page?
Adobe prototyped a tool that turns flat photos into walkable scenes
Testers kept walking back to the same unanswered corner
A tool now spots weak slides before clients do
Pick one deck slide and ask what hides beside it
thread_text:
1. Your deck has a blind spot

Adobe built a tool that turns flat photos into walkable 3D scenes. Testers kept walking back to the same unanswered corner—the one your slide hides.

2. Adobe's spatial prototype

It converts a single photo into a navigable scene. The surprise wasn't the tech—it was where people instinctively walked first.

3. The corner testers returned to

Every tester circled back to the same weak slide. The tool exposed a gap the presenter had stopped seeing after ten rehearsals.

4. Weak slides, caught early

A new tool flags thin arguments before clients do. It doesn't polish—it finds the slide that can't survive a follow-up question.

5. Ask what's beside it

Open your next deck and point at one slide: what question lives just off its edge? If you can't answer in ten seconds, that's your rewrite.
